_comment: Hydrocele and scrotal swellings. Same architecture as pneumonia and inguinal hernia: shared surgery and core skills carry the examination, this file adds the hydrocele mechanism, the scrotal differential matrix, ultrasound-led workup, urgency bands and repair decisions.
name: Hydrocele and scrotal swellings
fullName: Hydrocele and scrotal swellings: examination of the scrotum
oneLine: A painless scrotal swelling that transilluminates, and the mimics that must not be missed

chapters.title: Basics
chapters.blurb: What a hydrocele is, and what it is not

chapters.title: Patient particulars
chapters.blurb: Age sets the diagnosis before the story begins

skill.particulars.demographics.expect: Age carries unusual weight here. An infant with an intermittent swelling, a teenager with sudden pain, a young man with a heavy painless testis, and a man past forty with a slowly enlarging painless swelling each point to a different member of the scrotal list, so record the exact age and the tempo together.

chapters.title: History of presenting illness
chapters.blurb: Months of quiet growth, or hours of sudden pain

skill.hx.chief_complaints.expect: Expect a story told in months: a painless scrotal swelling noticed by chance and growing slowly, heavy by evening but never truly painful. An acute story told in hours, with agony, vomiting or fever, belongs to torsion or infection, not to hydrocele.

skill.hx.surg.lump.expect: Ask where the swelling started, whether it changes on lying down or coughing, and whether passing urine alters it. A hydrocele starts below and stays below, does not vanish overnight, and is indifferent to micturition, while a hernia descends from above and a varicocele empties flat.

skill.hx.surg.scrotal_swelling_pain.expect: Characterise pain exactly, because its absence is the finding. A dull heaviness late in the day fits a large hydrocele; sharp sudden pain with vomiting fits torsion; burning urine with discharge points to epididymo-orchitis ascending from below.

chapters.title: Past, personal, drug and family history
chapters.blurb: The background that reframes the lump

chapters.title: General examination
chapters.blurb: A well man, unless the scrotum says otherwise

skill.gen.appearance.expect: Expect a comfortable, afebrile man in no distress. Fever, tachycardia or a toxic look argue against an uncomplicated hydrocele and toward infection, torsion or Fournier gangrene, each of which changes the urgency completely.

skill.gen.vitals.expect: Expect normal temperature, pulse and blood pressure. Fever with a red, tender scrotum marks epididymo-orchitis; severe pain with vomiting and a normal temperature still means torsion until proved otherwise, since torsion is a vascular event, not a febrile one.

chapters.title: Examination of the scrotum
chapters.blurb: Get above it, shine through it, then feel the testis

skill.exam.surg.scrotal_palpation.expect: Expect a cystic, fluctuant swelling wrapped around the lower pole and body of the testis, with the testis itself impalpable inside a tense hydrocele. If the testis is felt apart from the swelling, above and in front of it, the swelling is not a hydrocele at all.

skill.exam.surg.transillumination_scrotu.expect: Expect a brilliant red glow through the whole swelling when the torch is placed on its side in a darkened room. An opaque swelling after trauma suggests haematocele, and a solid non-translucent testis with a small reactive effusion suggests tumour.

skill.exam.surg.hernia_palpation.expect: Expect to get above the swelling, with fingers meeting over a normal cord, and no expansile impulse on coughing. Failure to get above it means the swelling descends from the abdomen, which is a hernia until proved otherwise.

skill.exam.surg.cord_swelling_traction.expect: Expect a normal cord felt separately above the swelling. A cyst confined to the cord that moves down when the testis is pulled is an encysted hydrocele of the cord, not a vaginal hydrocele, and it needs an inguinal approach.

skill.exam.surg.varicocele.expect: Expect no bag of worms and no thrill in an uncomplicated hydrocele. Where dilated veins are present, feel them standing and supine: a varicocele empties flat, and one of sudden onset in a middle aged man obliges you to examine the kidney.

skill.exam.surg.acute_scrotum_torsion.expect: In a chronic painless swelling expect none of the torsion signs: no sudden agony, no high tender transverse testis, no vomiting. Run through the checklist anyway, because missing torsion is the one error that costs a testis, and a hydrocele never explains acute pain.

skill.exam.surg.regional_nodes.expect: Expect no inguinal nodes in an uncomplicated hydrocele, and remember the testis drains to the para-aortic nodes, not the groin. Enlarged hard nodes above the umbilicus or at the left supraclavicular fossa point to a testicular tumour with spread.

The swelling was tense, tender and opaque after a recent blow. How does your management change?

examinerQuestions: His story is eight months of painless enlargement with no urinary symptoms. What single background fact would most reframe this swelling?

skill.reasoning.scrotal.basics.title: What a hydrocele is
skill.reasoning.scrotal.basics.oneLine: Clear fluid inside the sac that wraps the testis, and whether that sac still talks to the abdomen
skill.reasoning.scrotal.basics.why: A hydrocele is fluid where it should not be, inside a sac that should be closed. Knowing which sac holds the fluid, and whether it still communicates with the abdomen, decides between watching, scanning and operating.

teach.heading: Fluid inside the tunica, not inside the testis
teach.body:
The testis hangs inside a double layered pouch, the tunica vaginalis, left behind when the testis descended from the abdomen before birth. A vaginal hydrocele is a collection of clear serous fluid inside that pouch, around the front and sides of the testis, so the testis itself sits hidden within the fluid.

It forms when the pouch secretes more fluid than it absorbs. Most adult hydroceles are primary, meaning no disease of the testis or epididymis explains them. A secondary hydrocele holds the same fluid, but poured out in reaction to infection, trauma, torsion or a tumour, and there it is the reaction, not the fluid, that matters.

teach.heading: The family of hydroceles

rows: Comes and goes; empties on lying down
Sac distended to the deep ring, no link above
Fixed swelling in a child, not always in infancy
Cord swelling, easily mistaken for a hernia
Small cord cyst; traction test positive

teach.heading: Why infants and adults take different roads
teach.body:
In infants a communicating hydrocele comes and goes with posture and crying, and most settle on their own within the first year or two of life. Operating before that window closes treats many children who would have recovered without surgery.

In adults a primary hydrocele neither resolves nor stays small: it persists and usually enlarges over months to years, sometimes to the knee. A secondary hydrocele follows the opposite rule and settles once its cause is treated, which is why naming the cause is the whole diagnosis.

probes.q: Define a vaginal hydrocele in one sentence.
probes.a: A collection of clear serous fluid inside the tunica vaginalis, around the testis.

probes.q: How does a primary hydrocele differ from a secondary one?
probes.a: A primary hydrocele has no underlying testicular or epididymal disease and is often tense; a secondary hydrocele is a reactive effusion from infection, trauma, torsion or tumour and is usually lax.

probes.q: A two year old has an intermittent scrotal swelling that vanishes overnight. What is it, and what do you advise?
probes.a: A congenital communicating hydrocele through a patent passage. Advise observation with a fixed review date, since most resolve within the first year or two; refer to paediatric surgery if the swelling persists beyond that window, grows tense or appears on the other side, and examine the abdomen for ascites in bilateral cases.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.reasoning.scrotal.signs.title: The hydrocele picture
skill.reasoning.scrotal.signs.oneLine: Get above it, shine through it, and read what the testis is telling you
skill.reasoning.scrotal.signs.why: Two bedside tests, getting above the swelling and transillumination, separate a hydrocele from every mimic in under a minute. Each test answers one anatomical question, and the pattern of answers is the diagnosis.

teach.heading: The two cardinal signs
teach.body:
Fluctuation is tested sideways, because the scrotum is too mobile for the usual method. Steady the upper pole between thumb and fingers to make the sac tense, then press the lower pole: the displaced fluid pushes your upper fingers apart. The test proves free fluid, not the diagnosis, since any cystic swelling fluctuates.

Translucency is tested in darkness with a pencil torch on the side of the swelling, never behind it where the testis blocks the light. A clear hydrocele and an epididymal cyst glow red throughout; a spermatocele stays dark because its milky fluid is not clear, and blood or tumour stay dark.

teach.heading: Get above it, then read the testis
teach.body:
Slide your fingers above the swelling. In a pure hydrocele they meet over a normal cord: you can get above it. In a hernia they cannot, because the swelling continues into the abdomen. This single move divides purely scrotal swellings from inguinoscrotal ones.

Then read the testis. Impalpable within a tense sac fits a large primary hydrocele, but it also hides a tumour, so it obliges a scan. A testis felt apart from the swelling, above and behind it, means the lump is an epididymal cyst. A heavy, smooth, enlarged testis with fading sensation means tumour until proved otherwise.

teach.heading: Tense versus lax, and what each warns
teach.body:
A primary hydrocele is tense, stands forward, and irons out the rugosity of the scrotal skin with prominent veins. A secondary hydrocele is usually lax, and the testis and epididymis can still be felt through it, which is why laxity should prompt a search for infection, a tumour or old trauma.

Redness, heat and exquisite tenderness mean infection or torsion, never an uncomplicated hydrocele. A tense swelling after a blow that stays dark on transillumination is a haematocele, and old blood in the sac mimics tumour so closely that only a scan separates them.

probes.q: Name the two cardinal signs of a hydrocele.
What does getting above the swelling prove?
probes.a: That the swelling is purely scrotal and has no connection with the abdomen; failure to get above it means it descends from above, which is a hernia until proved otherwise.

probes.q: The swelling transilluminates but the testis cannot be felt. What do you do next, and why?
probes.a: Arrange a scrotal ultrasound to assess the testis, because a tumour can hide behind a reactive hydrocele and the hand cannot clear it.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.reasoning.scrotal.differential.title: Differential diagnosis of the scrotal swelling
skill.reasoning.scrotal.differential.oneLine: Every swelling that shares the scrotum, and the one test that separates each
skill.reasoning.scrotal.differential.why: Most painless swellings are exactly what they look like, but the ones that are not are dangerous to miss: a tumour hiding behind reactive fluid, torsion masquerading as infection, and a hernia mistaken for a hydrocele. The differential does not stop once fluid is found.

teach.heading: Swelling by swelling

rows: Cannot get above; expansile impulse; resonant
Reduce, occlude the deep ring, re-examine
Heavy smooth testis; sensation lost; painless
Felt apart above the testis; brilliantly clear
Lax cyst above and behind the testis, felt apart from it; does not transilluminate
Ultrasound showing a cyst separate from the testis
Bag of worms; empties lying; thrill on coughing
Doppler; examine the kidney if sudden
Teenager; sudden agony; high tender testis
Fever; red hot scrotum; epididymis tender first
Recent blow or tap; tense, tender, opaque
Periodic fever with an opaque swelling; negative translucency test

teach.heading: Three presentations that must never wait
teach.body:
Sudden agonising scrotal pain with vomiting in a boy or young man is torsion until proved otherwise. If the diagnosis is in doubt, explore: a needless exploration harms little, while a missed torsion costs the testis within hours.

An impalpable testis inside any swelling mandates an ultrasound to exclude tumour before any reassurance or any needle. A rapidly enlarging, tense or blood stained swelling after trauma mandates urgent surgical review for haematocele with possible testicular rupture.

teach.heading: Where the swelling sits decides the list
teach.body:
First divide purely scrotal swellings, which you can get above, from inguinoscrotal ones, which you cannot. The cord then gets its own examination: a cyst confined to the cord that descends when the testis is pulled down is an encysted hydrocele of the cord, while a soft doughy cord swelling that fills slowly from below is a lymph varix of filariasis.

Remember the drainage: scrotal skin goes to the groin nodes, but the testis and epididymis drain to the para-aortic nodes at the transpyloric plane. Groin nodes therefore clear the skin, not the testis, and a testicular tumour is staged by examining the abdomen, not the groin.

probes.q: Name four differentials of a painless scrotal swelling.
probes.a: Inguinoscrotal hernia, testicular tumour, epididymal cyst or spermatocele, and varicocele.

probes.q: How do you separate an epididymal cyst from a hydrocele at the bedside?
probes.a: The cyst is felt apart from the testis, above and behind it, while the hydrocele surrounds the testis and hides it; an epididymal cyst glows red throughout, while a spermatocele stays dark because its milky fluid is not clear.

probes.q: A young man has a painless heavy testis with a small non-translucent effusion. What is your working diagnosis and next step?
probes.a: A testicular tumour with a reactive secondary hydrocele. Arrange urgent scrotal ultrasound with tumour markers, examine the abdomen for para-aortic nodes, and refer to urology without delay or scrotal violation.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery
sources.locator: The testes and scrotum: differential diagnosis of scrotal swellings

skill.investigation.scrotal.workup.title: Investigating the scrotal swelling
skill.investigation.scrotal.workup.oneLine: The scan clears the testis; the rest of the workup hunts the cause
skill.investigation.scrotal.workup.why: Investigations in a scrotal swelling serve two separate jobs: proving the testis underneath is normal, and finding the cause when the fluid is secondary. Knowing which test does which job stops a student scanning every simple hydrocele and missing every tumour.

teach.heading: Bedside tests come first
teach.body:
Fluctuation and transillumination are investigations in their own right, not preliminaries. Perform them the same way every time: steady the upper pole for fluctuation, darken the room and place the torch on the side of the swelling for translucency, and record each as positive or negative.

Repeat transillumination after any change in the swelling. A hydrocele that stops transilluminating has gained blood, pus or a thickened sac, and each of those restarts the workup rather than ending it.

teach.heading: Ultrasound is the arbiter
teach.body:
Order a scrotal ultrasound whenever the testis cannot be felt, when a secondary cause is suspected, after trauma, with rapid growth, or with blood stained fluid. It shows anechoic fluid around a normal testis in a simple hydrocele, and a mass, septations or a ruptured tunica when something else is present.

Add colour Doppler when torsion or varicocele is in question: absent flow marks torsion, refluxing veins mark varicocele. Ultrasound is available at most district hospitals and medical colleges; where it is not, refer rather than guess, and never substitute a needle for the scan.

teach.heading: Look for the cause, not for numbers
teach.body:
Examine the urine routinely with culture when there is burning, frequency, discharge or epididymal tenderness, since ascending infection is the commonest treatable cause of a secondary effusion. Where filariasis is suspected, check the blood for eosinophilia and examine a night smear for microfilariae.

Request a chest film with tuberculosis contact or suspected testicular spread, and tumour markers, namely alpha fetoprotein, beta human chorionic gonadotrophin and lactate dehydrogenase, only when imaging raises concern for malignancy. A classic transilluminant hydrocele with a normal testis on the scan needs none of these.

teach.heading: Aspiration diagnoses nothing
teach.body:
A diagnostic tap risks infection, bleeding into the sac and, in a tumour, spread along the needle track, while telling you less than the scan already did. Reserve aspiration for relieving a tense swelling in a patient unfit for surgery, with clear counselling that fluid usually reaccumulates.

Note the fluid only when it is already drawn: amber and clear in a simple hydrocele, milky in chylocele or spermatocele, blood stained in haematocele or tumour. Blood stained fluid, whenever seen, needs urgent ultrasound rather than reassurance, with markers and urology referral when imaging raises concern for malignancy.

probes.q: When is scrotal ultrasound mandatory in a hydrocele?
probes.a: Whenever the testis cannot be palpated, or a secondary cause such as tumour, trauma or infection is suspected.

probes.q: Which tumour markers are requested, and when?
probes.a: Alpha fetoprotein, beta human chorionic gonadotrophin and lactate dehydrogenase, only when imaging or examination raises concern for testicular malignancy.

probes.q: A patient unfit for surgery asks for repeated aspiration instead of an operation. What do you tell him?
probes.a: That aspiration relieves but rarely cures, fluid usually returns, each tap carries infection and bleeding risk, and the testis must first be cleared by ultrasound so a tumour is not missed.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery
sources.locator: The testes and scrotum: investigation of scrotal disease

skill.reasoning.scrotal.diagnosis.title: Diagnosis and urgency of the scrotal swelling
skill.reasoning.scrotal.diagnosis.oneLine: Name the variety, then place it on the urgency ladder
skill.reasoning.scrotal.diagnosis.why: A diagnosis of hydrocele says nothing about what happens next unless it names the variety and the urgency. An infant communicating hydrocele is watched, a large tense primary is listed, and an acute painful scrotum goes to theatre tonight, all under the same word.

teach.heading: The complete diagnostic statement
teach.body:
A full diagnosis names the variety, the side, the course and the complications in one breath: a primary vaginal hydrocele of the right testis, present eight months, uncomplicated. Each word earns its place, because secondary, bilateral or complicated changes the plan.

The criteria for a primary vaginal hydrocele are a painless, fluctuant, translucent swelling from which one can get above, with the testis impalpable but normal on ultrasound and no cough impulse. Miss one criterion and the label must change, not stretch.

teach.heading: Three urgency bands

rows: Small lax painless swelling; testis normal on scan
Reassure, support, review if it grows
Large tense swelling with heaviness; doubt about the testis
Scan, then list for elective repair
Acute pain, trauma with opaque swelling, red hot scrotum with fever
Emergency exploration or referral without delay

teach.heading: When the label must change
teach.body:
A swelling that does not transilluminate is not a simple hydrocele: think haematocele after trauma, pus in a suppurating sac, or tumour with a small reactive effusion. A swelling felt apart from the testis is a cyst of the epididymis or a spermatocele.

Any expansile cough impulse reclassifies the case as a hernia, however scrotal it looks. Sudden pain reclassifies everything as the acute scrotum, where torsion is assumed until excluded, and no hydrocele ever explains agony of sudden onset.

probes.q: State a complete diagnosis for a classic case.
probes.a: A primary vaginal hydrocele of the right testis, present eight months, uncomplicated.

probes.q: Which findings place a scrotal swelling in the tonight band?
probes.a: Sudden severe pain with vomiting, a tense opaque swelling after trauma, or fever with a red tender scrotum, pointing to torsion, rupture or suppuration.

probes.q: The swelling transilluminates but an impulse appears on coughing. What is the diagnosis?
probes.a: An inguinoscrotal hernia, possibly with a coexisting hydrocele; the impulse proves a connection with the abdomen, so the hydrocele label alone is wrong.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.treatment.scrotal.management.title: Managing hydrocele and its causes
skill.treatment.scrotal.management.oneLine: Watch the infants, repair the large, treat the cause underneath
skill.treatment.scrotal.management.why: No hydrocele heals itself except the infant communicating kind, yet not every hydrocele needs an operation. The art is matching the variety to its road: observation, planned repair, urgent exploration, or treatment of the infection, filariasis or tumour that poured the fluid.

teach.heading: Watch the infants, reassure the mild
teach.body:
Observe a communicating hydrocele in infancy, since most resolve within the first year or two as the passage closes. Review the child if the swelling persists beyond that window, grows tense, or the other side swells, and operate then by ligating the passage through the groin.

Reassure the adult with a small, soft, asymptomatic primary hydrocele. Explain its benign nature, advise a suspensory support for heavy days, and fix a review if it enlarges, aching begins, or any red flag appears. Observation is a decision, not neglect, and it needs a date attached.

teach.heading: Repair the large and symptomatic
teach.body:
Offer surgery for a large, tense or heavy hydrocele, one that limits walking, work or intercourse, or any swelling where doubt about the testis remains after scanning. The standard operations open the scrotum and deal with the sac by excision with eversion or by plication behind the testis.

Counsel before listing: recurrence is uncommon after sac surgery but haematoma, infection and chronic aching occur, and fertility is unaffected. Most repairs run as day care under spinal or local anaesthesia in a government hospital, often covered under public insurance schemes, with a week of support and wound watch after.

teach.heading: Treat the cause in every secondary hydrocele
teach.body:
Rest, elevation, scrotal support and guideline chosen antimicrobials settle epididymo-orchitis, alongside treatment of the urethritis or urinary infection that fed it. Tuberculosis needs a full antitubercular course with urology follow up, since the epididymis, vas and seminal vesicles scar together.

Filariasis needs an antifilarial course by the national guideline with the hydrocele repaired after the infection settles. A testicular tumour goes to urology for inguinal orchidectomy with marker and staging workup; never biopsy or drain through the scrotum. Aspiration with sclerotherapy is reserved for patients unfit for surgery, with explicit warning that fluid usually returns.

teach.heading: After the operation and the safety net
teach.body:
Discharge with a suspensory bandage, wound care advice and a date for stitch and swelling review. Warn that some oedema and bruising are expected, but fever, spreading redness, a rapidly enlarging haematoma or foul discharge mean an early return.

Give every patient the three red flags in plain words: sudden severe pain with vomiting, rapid tense enlargement, and fever with a red scrotum each need same day reassessment. Record what was told, because the patient who understands the flags returns in time.

probes.q: Which hydroceles can be watched rather than operated?
probes.a: Communicating hydroceles in infants, most resolving within the first year or two, and small asymptomatic primary hydroceles in adults with a normal testis on scan.

probes.q: What operations are offered for a large primary vaginal hydrocele?
probes.a: Scrotal excision of the sac with eversion, or plication of the sac behind the testis; a communicating hydrocele in a child is instead ligated through the groin.

probes.q: A hydrocele follows proven tuberculous epididymitis. Outline management.
probes.a: A full antitubercular course with urology follow up, scrotal support and review of the swelling as treatment proceeds, repairing the hydrocele only after the infection has settled and the testis is reassessed.

cases.title: A bus conductor with a slowly enlarging scrotal swelling
cases.opening: Ramesh Yadav, 46, has come to the surgery outpatient clinic with a swelling of the right scrotum that has grown over eight months. He is afebrile and in no pain. Take a history and examine him.
cases.fallback: I am not sure what you mean, doctor. Can you ask that a different way?

patient.name: Ramesh Yadav
patient.occupation: Bus conductor on the town route
patient.residence: Small town, lives with his wife and two children

cues: what brings you here today
tell me about the swelling in the scrotum
what is the main problem today
presenting.reply: Doctor, for eight months there is a swelling in my right scrotum. It keeps growing slowly. There is no pain, only a heaviness by evening.

cues: when did the swelling first appear
how did the lump start in the scrotum
was the onset sudden or gradual
swelling_onset_course.reply: It began small, like a lemon, on the right side eight months back. It has grown steadily since, and never went away on its own.

cues: how has the size changed over months
how big is the swelling now
has the swelling grown since you first noticed it
swelling_size_progress.reply: It is now the size of a small mango. It grows a little every month. It hangs lower than the left side.

cues: do you get pain in the swelling
tell me about the heaviness in the scrotum
is the swelling painful to touch
scrotal_pain_character.reply: No real pain, doctor. By evening after a full day of standing it feels heavy and drags. Touching it does not hurt.

cues: does the swelling bulge when you cough
what happens to the lump on coughing or straining
does the swelling come down from above
cough_impulse_noticed.reply: No, coughing makes no difference. It does not come down from above; it has always been only in the scrotum.

cues: does the swelling disappear on lying down
what happens to the lump when you lie flat at night
is the swelling smaller in the morning
lying_down_effect.reply: It stays the same, doctor. Lying down at night makes no difference; in the morning it is exactly as it was.

cues: do you have burning on passing urine
tell me about your urine stream and frequency
any difficulty in passing urine
urinary_burning_stream.reply: No burning, no difficulty. I pass urine normally, two or three times in the day and once at night.

cues: have you had any urethral discharge
any treatment for infection after physical relations
any sores or discharge from the private parts
discharge_exposure_history.reply: No, doctor, nothing like that. I have never taken treatment for such an infection.

cues: have you injured the scrotum
any blow or hurt to the private parts
did the swelling follow an accident
trauma_blow_history.reply: No injury at all. I only noticed it one day while bathing. No tap or draining has been done.

cues: have you had fever with a painful swollen cord
tell me about attacks of fever with scrotal pain
any swelling of the legs with fever
filarial_fever_history.reply: No, I have never had such fever. My legs have never swollen. We have lived in this town all our lives.

cues: has anyone at home had tuberculosis
anyone in the family coughing for months
were you ever treated for tuberculosis
tuberculosis_contact_history.reply: No, nobody at home has TB, and I have never taken TB medicines.

cues: did you have mumps in childhood
any painful swelling of the testis as a boy
did you have swelling below the ears with fever as a child
mumps_childhood_history.reply: I had the usual childhood fevers, but never a painful swelling of the testis that I remember.

cues: what work do you do each day
how many hours do you stand at work
tell me about your duty as a conductor
standing_work_hours.reply: I am a bus conductor on the town route. I stand in the moving bus nearly ten hours a day, six days a week.

cues: do you smoke beedis or cigarettes
since when do you use tobacco
do you chew tobacco as well
beedi_tobacco_history.reply: I smoke four or five beedis a day since I was twenty. No chewing tobacco. I drink only at festivals.

cues: which medicines do you take every day
are you on any blood thinner tablets
do you take tablets for sugar or pressure
daily_medicines_list.reply: Nothing daily, doctor. No sugar, no pressure tablets. Only an occasional paracetamol.

cues: do you have diabetes or blood pressure
any heart or lung disease I should know
any earlier operation on the abdomen or groin
other_illness_check.reply: No diabetes, no blood pressure. I have never been admitted to hospital or operated.

cues: has anyone in your family had a similar swelling
any groin or scrotal operation in the family
does your brother have a swelling like this
family_similar_swelling.reply: No, nobody in the family has had this. My father and brother are both well.

cues: has the swelling ever become suddenly painful
any vomiting with severe scrotal pain
has the lump ever turned red and hot
redflag_sudden_pain_swelling.reply: Never, doctor. It has never pained suddenly, never turned red, and I have never vomited with it.

skill.gen.appearance.finding: Comfortable middle aged man in no distress. Afebrile, no pallor, no lymphadenopathy on general look.

skill.gen.vitals.finding: Pulse 78 regular. Blood pressure 126/82. Respiratory rate 16. SpO2 98 percent on room air. Temperature 37.0 C.

skill.exam.surg.scrotal_palpation.finding: Pyriform cystic swelling of the right scrotum, cystic and fluctuant, skin free over it with lost rugosity. The testis cannot be felt apart from the swelling; the left testis and cord are normal.

skill.exam.surg.transillumination_scrotu.finding: Brilliantly translucent throughout with the torch on the side of the swelling in a darkened room. No opaque area.

skill.exam.surg.hernia_palpation.finding: One can get above the swelling with fingers meeting over a normal cord. No expansile impulse on coughing; the swelling does not reduce.

skill.exam.surg.varicocele.finding: No bag of worms on either side, standing or supine. No thrill on coughing over the cords.

skill.exam.surg.regional_nodes.finding: No inguinal lymphadenopathy on either side. Abdomen soft, no lump felt above the umbilicus.

usg_scrotum.label: Scrotal ultrasound
usg_scrotum.result: Anechoic fluid collection around the right testis measuring about 9 cm. Testis of normal size and echo texture, epididymis normal, no mass or septation. Left side normal.
usg_scrotum.note: This clears the testis inside the fluid, which the hand could not do. A normal testis on the scan is what lets you call this primary.

urine_routine.label: Urine routine and culture
urine_routine.note: Not indicated: no burning, frequency, discharge or epididymal tenderness, so no ascending infection to hunt.

blood_counts.label: Blood counts
blood_counts.note: Not indicated: no filarial fever, systemic upset or tuberculosis contact, and the scan already shows a normal testis.

tumour_markers.label: Tumour markers
tumour_markers.note: Not indicated: the swelling transilluminates fully and the scan shows a normal testis with no mass. Markers are for suspected malignancy, not for every hydrocele.

doppler_scrotum.label: Colour Doppler of the scrotum
doppler_scrotum.note: Not indicated: there is no pain, no sudden onset and no varicocele on examination, so there is no torsion or venous question to answer.

cxr.label: Chest radiograph
cxr.note: Not indicated: no tuberculosis contact, no urinary tuberculosis clue and no suspected testicular spread that would need lung staging.

differentialModel.answer: Primary vaginal hydrocele of the right testis. Consider an inguinoscrotal hernia, a varicocele, an epididymal cyst, a spermatocele, epididymo-orchitis, testicular torsion, a haematocele and a testicular tumour.

diagnosis.answer: Primary vaginal hydrocele of the right testis, present eight months, uncomplicated.

managementModel.answer: Reassure and explain the benign nature of the swelling, confirm the testis is normal on scrotal ultrasound, offer elective hydrocele repair for a swelling of this size with heaviness, advise scrotal support with review if pain or rapid enlargement occurs, and refer urgently if the testis cannot be assessed or red flags appear.
accept: reassure and explain the benign nature of the swelling
confirm the testis is normal on scrotal ultrasound
offer elective hydrocele repair for a large symptomatic swelling
advise scrotal support with review if pain or rapid enlargement occurs
refer urgently if the testis cannot be assessed or red flags appear

teachingPoints: The tempo alone should move you toward a hydrocele before a single test is run: eight months of painless growth, not the hours of torsion or the weeks of infection.
Getting above the swelling with no cough impulse divides a purely scrotal swelling from a hernia in one move, and it must never be skipped even when the swelling looks typical.
Brilliant translucency proves clear fluid, but it never clears the testis: the impalpable testis inside still obliges an ultrasound before reassurance.
Prolonged standing is the occupational background here, and it correctly raises varicocele in the history, but the examination refutes it: no bag of worms, no emptying flat, no thrill.

Urine and blood counts were rightly omitted here: with no burning, discharge, epididymal tenderness, filarial fever or tuberculosis contact, nothing justified them; each question was still asked because a positive answer would have changed the road.
A 9 cm tense swelling with evening heaviness in a working man has crossed from reassure to repair: size with symptoms is the indication, not size alone.
Aspiration was rightly not offered as a plan: it relieves but rarely cures, and each tap risks infection while the diagnosis still stands on the scan, not the syringe.
